Detrimental

/det-rih-MEN-tul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Detrimental means causing harm or damage.

Detrimental means causing harm or damage. Skipping warm-ups is detrimental to any athlete's joints, no matter how young or flexible.

Worked Example

The debate team met at 6 a.m., and attendance was slipping. Coach Ruiz surveyed the members and found most were sleeping fewer than six hours a night. She moved practice to after school the next week. 'Whatever we gained in quiet mornings,' she told the principal, 'the lost sleep was detrimental to their focus — the trade-off wasn't close.'

The early practices harmed the students' focus by costing them sleep — a straightforward case of something being detrimental.

How Detrimental Sits Among Its Neighbors

harmful

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — inconvenient → detrimental → ruinous

inconvenient vs. detrimental

inconvenient vs. detrimental: An inconvenient rule merely annoys people, while a detrimental one causes real harm.

ruinous vs. detrimental

ruinous vs. detrimental: Ruinous goes far beyond detrimental — harm so great it destroys entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: away, down (Latin)

Root — trim-

Root — trim-: to rub, to wear away (Latin terere; detrimentum, 'a wearing away, loss')

Suffix — -ental

Suffix — -ental: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: Detrimental comes from Latin detrimentum, 'a rubbing away, a loss,' built on de-, 'away,' plus terere, 'to rub or wear.' The same wearing-away root appears in attrition, the slow grinding down of a force or workforce. Detour shares only the prefix; its core comes from a different root meaning 'to turn.'

Use the root in a new word: attrition

Use the root in a new word: attrition: Armies and companies are worn down by attrition — from Latin terere, 'to rub or wear away,' the same root inside detrimental.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, general-purpose

Detrimental is the plainest, most neutral of this unit's harm words — use it whenever you simply mean 'causing harm.' Deleterious adds a hint of subtle or gradual damage, and destructive means the harm is massive, even total.
